scenario: AITA For going on my best friend's dream trip and not inviting her? | Me and Mandy have been best friends since basically kindergarten, and almost since then she's been fascinated with Turkey, Croatia, and the Balkans/Mediterranean region in general. I started dating a guy from a Balkan country and was making plans to go visit him and his family, and while doing so I found this AMAZING package deal that lets you travel the Balkans, Spain, Greece, Turkey and Morocco. Seriously, it was like a once in a lifetime deal and though it's pretty expensive, it's WAY cheaper than it would be to find places to stay and travel to those places on your own. I KNEW Mandy couldn't afford it, and I KNEW it would hurt her deeply that she wasn't getting a chance to go. This trip is literally what she dreams of doing, and with me in particular, but she's been in a lot of financial trouble lately. So I told her I was planning a trip, but not any of the details. I also told another very close friend about the trip, and she looked up the same deal and decided she wanted to go as well. I said I'd love to have the company, so she bought her tickets and she's coming along too. I realized that if Mandy heard about this or found out about this before I got a chance to tell her she'd be super hurt, so I told her about the trip. She was SOOOOOOO upset. She asked about why I didn't invite her, and I told her it was because I knew she couldn't afford it and I thought it would just be salt in the wound. (I also privately think she would have made some very questionable decisions in order to fund the trip, or would have gone and then not had enough for money, or her bills, or things like that at home.) That just made it worse, and she cried, and cried about how we always said we'd go and experience those places together, and that I don't even have any interest in the region, which is pretty much true since I want to travel around Asia. I told her we could still go that in the future, and we could even do this trip in the future, but she was too hurt to want to hear that. My boyfriend thinks I am being kind of a dick, and says for his best friend, he'd have offered to pay for part to help if he could, and I guess I \*could\* but not super comfortably and idk when she'd pay me back. He also thinks she'd have been less hurt if I brought it up while I was thinking about it. My other friend agrees that it was a good idea to wait to tell her since she agrees Mandy probably would have done ANYTHING to go on that trip.

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me start by understanding the situation.

The person in question is planning a big trip to several countries in the Balkans, Spain, Greece, Turkey, and Morocco. It's a once-in-a-lifetime deal that's expensive but cheaper than doing it on their own. They have a best friend, Mandy, who has always been fascinated with that region and has talked about going there together. However, the person knows that Mandy can't afford it right now because she's in financial trouble. They also think that if Mandy tried to go, she might make bad financial decisions or end up in worse financial shape.

So, the person decides not to invite Mandy on the trip. Instead, they tell another close friend about the trip, and that friend joins them. Then, they tell Mandy about the trip, which upsets her a lot. She's hurt because they didn't invite her and because they didn't seem interested in the region she loves. The person tried to comfort her by saying they could go in the future, but Mandy was too upset to accept that.

The person's boyfriend thinks they were being a bit harsh and suggests that they could have offered to help pay for Mandy's trip, even if it wasn't comfortable. He also thinks that bringing up the trip earlier might have been better. The other friend agrees that waiting to tell Mandy was a good idea because she would have done anything to go.

Now, I need to evaluate whether the action of not inviting Mandy on the trip is morally acceptable. Let's break it down.

First, the person didn't invite Mandy because they knew she couldn't afford it and didn't want to hurt her. That seems kind because they were trying to protect her feelings. But by not inviting her, they ended up hurting her anyway when she found out. So, their intention was good, but the outcome was negative.

Second, the person told another friend about the trip, and that friend joined them. That might have been a good idea because having a travel buddy can make the trip more enjoyable. But it also means that Mandy felt excluded, especially since she was their best friend.

Third, the person's boyfriend suggested offering to help pay for Mandy's trip. The person could have done that but didn't because it wasn't comfortable. That might have been a better approach because it would have shown more support for Mandy's dream.

Fourth, the person didn't bring up the trip earlier, which might have given Mandy a chance to express her feelings or find a way to go. By waiting, they made the situation worse when Mandy found out.

So, considering all these points, the action of not inviting Mandy seems to have good intentions but led to negative outcomes. The person tried to protect Mandy's feelings but ended up hurting her more. They also didn't consider offering financial help or discussing the trip earlier, which could have been better approaches.

Therefore, I think the action is morally unacceptable because, despite the good intentions, it caused significant harm to the friendship and didn't fully consider Mandy's feelings and needs.
